latitude.why: Surface (transient strip vs modal vs persistent badge), open semantics (new window vs in-place swap), display order, and overflow policy are all reviewer-debatable; only flock ownership, the adoption default, and env-free operation are forced.

q1.position: A transient first-paint strip at the top of the adopted window, plus a full session-picker overlay on Ctrl+Shift+S, wired as a pane chord with a window-level fallback like Ctrl+Shift+A.
q1.rationale: The ticket's own sketch; help-modal and agent-watch overlays already establish both patterns, and Ctrl+Shift+S is unclaimed.

q2.position: Passive: the strip paints automatically at launch whenever other free sessions exist, naming them; it dismisses on keystroke, click, or roughly eight seconds. The chord plus an F1 help row remain afterwards.
q2.rationale: Silence breaks at first paint, exactly where #196 locates the defect; nothing to discover before you see it.

q3.position: Per row: session id, pane count, and saved time (clock time if today, date otherwise) — e.g. '7 · 2 panes · 19:04'. All from scan_sessions' existing Candidate fields.
q3.rationale: Matches the sketch; id, panes and mtime are already read cheaply, so no deeper TOML parsing enters the boot path.

q4.position: Launch adopts newest; strip lists the rest; click a row, or chord then arrows then Enter. TD spawns a detached self-process with TD_SESSION=<id> (demo-spawn pattern); that window claims and restores the session.
q4.rationale: Reuses the existing explicit-session boot path end to end; no mid-run restore machinery is written.

q5.position: Nothing changes: the current window keeps its adopted session and the chosen one opens as a new window, matching the one-window-per-session model instance.rs is built around.
q5.rationale: The module doc treats sessions as windows on a tiling desktop; swapping in place would fight that model.

q6.position: Yes — the existing per-id flock in claim_in stays the sole arbiter. The picker lists only free sessions via a non-stealing flock probe; losing the spawn race opens a scratch window that says why.
q6.rationale: The kernel lock already guarantees single ownership; the UI filters, it never arbitrates.

q7.position: Zero other free sessions — which includes the exactly-one case, since launch adopts it — paints no strip. The chord still opens the picker, showing a 'no other saved sessions' empty state.
q7.rationale: Affordance appears only when actionable; the chord stays discoverable and self-explaining.

q8.position: The exact rank() order — workspace hint, substantial, recency, id tiebreak — with the adopted session removed. The strip's first row is precisely what the launch would have adopted next.
q8.rationale: One ordering rule for adoption and display; this hooks rank() without reordering its policy.

q9.position: The strip shows at most 3 sessions, then a '+N more — Ctrl+Shift+S' tail; the picker overlay scrolls the full ranked list with no cap.
q9.rationale: Three rows fit one strip without stealing terminal rows; the overlay absorbs any long tail.

q10.position: Stateless: scan_sessions reruns at every paint of the strip and every picker open; nothing new is persisted. Strip dismissal lives only in process memory for this run.
q10.rationale: The tomls and locks on disk are already the truth; caching or persisting a copy invites staleness.

q11.position: Yes: click a strip row, or chord plus Enter. TD_SESSION is set only inside the spawner's child environment; the user never types or exports an environment variable.
q11.rationale: Internal reuse of the existing mechanism keeps one boot path while meeting the ticket's no-env-var bar.

q12.position: Yes — resolve_session is untouched; the strip renders after adoption completes and changes nothing about which session was claimed or how.
q12.rationale: The ticket scopes ranking-policy changes out; this plan only reads what adoption already decided.
